runs.answer: Prices go up when more people want something than there is to go around. Imagine a candy bar sells out fast because everyone wants one. The shop owner notices and raises the price a little. Some people decide it's not worth it and buy something else, and the candy gets bought by those who want it most. Higher prices help balance supply and demand!

Imagine you have a lemonade stand, but instead of lemonade, you sell candy bars. Each candy bar costs you 50 cents to make, and you sell each one for 75 cents. Everyone is happy, and you're making a little money on each one!

Then one day, the sugar you buy gets more expensive. Now each candy bar costs you 80 cents to make. If you keep selling them for 75 cents, you'd lose money on every bar! So you have to raise your price to 90 cents to keep your candy stand going.

That's one reason prices go up: it costs more to make things.

Here's another reason. Suppose kids all over town suddenly want your candy bars. Maybe there was a big sports game and everyone is craving something sweet.
